chapter: Riverboat to New Orleans and Horace Henderson
title: Playing on percentage; Roy leaves, Granger and guitarist Luke Stewart join
summary: With Horace they played for a split of the door instead of the boat's guaranteed $40; after Roy left Granger was sent for, and Louisville guitarist Luke Stewart, who later played with Stuff Smith, was also in the band.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: Well, the only thing that was different on this job, the job on the boat you made money. See, with Horace you could play and he'd give you 25 cents and you'd split it up. You've got to take it. See he was playing on percentage. See, I got a good taste of it when I was on that boat. You got your $40.00 every week, no excuse.
And your room and board, you know.
So I'm out here now, I'm glad to play with these guys, you know. Because Roy, it was about the first band he played in too.

Yes, so he was there. And he was the man with the solos, and Red played first and Bernice played first. Well then I went in, after Red left, there was me and Bernice and Roy, and then finally Roy, I think Roy left, and they asked me was there another trumpet player down there, and I said yes, Granger. So then he sent for Granger. So Granger come in, and then we had another guy from Louisville played the guitar, beautiful guitar, a guy named Luke Stewart. Did you ever hear of him?
Played with Stuff in the later days with Stuff's band. Around about '38. And he was pretty good, because he and Charlie Christian tied up in Kelly's Stable one night, you know.
He was a great guy, a great guitar. Yeah, he's in Buffalo now.
